findings.title: CCU did not adequately pursue potential wage garnishments from debtors.
findings.description: CCU did not always pursue wage garnishments on viable accounts identified through quarterly computer matches despite policies considering debts over $750. Testing showed delays or lack of referral to the Legal Measures Unit without documentation for several debtor accounts. Similar conditions have been noted in six preceding audit reports since 1997.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DBM take appropriate action to pursue potential wage garnishments from debtors in a timely manner and document all collection efforts (repeat). For example, DBM should consider supplementing CCU’s debt collection policies to provide guidance on prioritizing accounts for potential wage garnishments.

findings.title: Controls over system access and sensitive personally identifiable information were not sufficient.
findings.description: CCU operated the Revenue Plus Collection System with approximately 1,500 users having unnecessary direct file modification access to critical programs and data files. A critical file contained approximately one million unique social security numbers in clear text without encryption.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DBM a. restrict access to critical program and data files to only those users requiring such access (repeat); and b. encrypt all files containing sensitive personally identifiable information.

extraction.agency_response_summary: DBM CCU agrees with both findings and recommendations. For Finding 1, they expanded staff to file more suits/garnishments and will document efforts and establish prioritization guidelines. For Finding 2, they removed unnecessary user access and utilize encryption tools, with a new system planned for full encryption by end of 2017.
